hypothesis: write_file_atomic's unconditional sync_all diverges from TS writeFileAtomicSync's per-call-site fsync option, and persist_supervisor_config (the daemon's ONLY pre-bind durable write, a zero-reader mirror the boot rewrites anyway) carries a TS-absent fsync: TS persistSupervisorConfig passes NO fsync option, so the port's sync_all is added durability the product does not have. The pre-bind fsync rides the bind-span, and the settle leg2 (perf-settle-daemoninit3 decompose, relayed by the orchestrator) proved the bind-span is LEG-INLINE on every daemon-booting create path (spawn->bind p50 71.3ms on the settle host, ~92% durable-write not CPU; the persist's fresh write 34-37ms inline on that host class). L1 = drop the TS-absent fsync from the supervisor-config persist; expected win = the persist's fresh-write class cost off the bind-span of every daemon-booting create path, regime-relative (34-37ms on the settle host's healthy class; whatever the host's fresh-write class costs where it runs).
approach: Branch lane/perf-daemon-lazyinit-l1-prebuild, base 3358e0016 (org/main = origin/main), 3 commits, ONE file crates/pa-daemon/src/descriptor.rs, +87/-4: (722c56625) TempSync{Synced,Unsynced} enum documenting TS writeFileAtomicSync's per-call-site fsync option + write_file_atomic keeps Synced for every existing caller + new pub(crate) write_file_atomic_unsynced + persist_supervisor_config switched to the unsynced shape with the TS call-site parity documented; (edb083daf) the round-trip test compares fields (the struct is not PartialEq); (92cc1c7a9) rustfmt tuple shape. Two new tests: the unsynced rename replaces the destination and leaves no temp; the persisted supervisor config round-trips through the unsynced write and belongs to its socket. Measurement: the prebuilt same-VM sequential ABAB pair (leg_abba.py, n=12/leg-instance, 2 leg instances per letter = 24/letter, shapes prewarmed+inline, sha-asserted atomic binary swaps, spin calib pre/mid/post, 1ms-grid floor probe, I/O advisory v1.0 regime probes at EVERY leg boundary, PI_OFFLINE=1 disclosed, idle gates, SIGTERM reap + leftover-poison check). Served-path contract (served_path.py) on both binaries: hello normalized byte-identity, first create, post-shutdown supervisor-config present+parseable+socket-bound (the L1 served path).
parity_notes: A CONVERGENCE, not a divergence: TS writeFileAtomicSync's WriteFileAtomicOptions.fsync is a per-call-site opt-in, and TS persistSupervisorConfig passes only {mode:0o600} — no fsync — so unsynced is the TS posture at exactly this call site. Every other write_file_atomic caller (worker descriptors, identity-pending record: the durable surfaces) keeps the Synced shape — zero behavior change outside the supervisor-config mirror. Frozen surfaces proven: the hello line's normalized form byte-identical base-vs-patched (sha 194f312b250bdcffff3eb67b5879e333f42a8dcaace8c5c6bac94146ed73cacc both sides, volatile fields dropped incl. per-trial socket paths). Served-path contract PASS on both binaries: the unsynced atomic write still lands the supervisor-config mirror (present + version-1 parseable + socketPath-bound at runtime), first create OK both sides. Crash story: a lost unsynced write costs the mirror this boot rewrote anyway (the module doc states it); readers only ever see parseable states through the atomic rename.
